title: Research: prove a sharp S4 coordinate-cut gap for mixed targets
body:
Ross Richardson's [common-certificate handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2570#discussioncomment-18956828) asks whether nonnegative coordinate-cut rank combinations on finite S4 permutation modules can prove the direct tariff for all 24 targets. A five-point pentagonal inequality rules this out: for `(2143,3142,4231,2143)`, their exact upper envelope is `8 beta + 4 alpha`, while separate scalar shortest words cost `9 beta + 3 alpha`, throughout `0 <= alpha <= beta`. At prices `(2,1,2)`, the sharp method bound is 20 versus direct cost 21. An existing ordered-pair/natural-cut combination attains the envelope.

This is a scoped proof-method obstruction. The actual arbitrary-dirty-workspace circuit optimum remains 20 or 21. Arbitrary subspace cuts and nonpermutation representations are outside the proof. No cheaper word, supplier or new kappa is claimed. The package includes the written argument, exact receipt, task/overlap metadata, explicit replay registration and authenticated verbatim predecessor proof/README/license.

Validation passed locally on Windows / CPython 3.12.10:

- `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/s4-two-premium-cut-envelope`: primary checker, separate right-action Floyd-Warshall oracle and six behavioral groups. Checks cover all 32 binary patterns, 24 scalar words, 1,093 undeduplicated words, 120 exact price comparisons, six-role formal endpoints and twelve call omissions. Four producer mutants, an independent orientation mutant, source drift and corrupted evidence reject.
- Direct optimized CPython 3.14.6 and Git-free read-only normal/optimized exports pass.
- `python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/s4-two-premium-cut-envelope`: all 15 package/input files match `3aa400ed59d19b9d6c08e22d1b75edb36a1d3e27`; `git diff --check` passes. No full supplier replay, hosted CI pass, independent human review or formal-kernel proof is claimed.

Scientific base `b3f3ee0392b71b118fd086a6eaf6b4cab54ef455`, chooser nonce `428618959ce92654afec0b1fcbcac0de`, priority revision 5. Rebased onto current main `836b19bfa309ceafbc8ee32a15e8c4b10dde7e11` after reading revision-6 guidance; this bit card and all mathematical inputs are unchanged. Submission overlap refreshed 238 open PRs and 1,704 Discussion records plus local notes/ledger; coverage limits are recorded. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2570#discussioncomment-18977830).

Next: analyze equality in the inherited unit-price/natural cuts. Any cost-20 word must have exactly twelve total and eight exterior calls. Further coordinate-cut enumeration cannot close this gap; no larger word search is undertaken here.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR2583; Ross Richardson's cut-cone archive (`ebba00f3`) and PR1966/1989; Adam Gall/PR1941; David Arias/PR2738; complementary PR2577; and Jerry Chen's related abelian metric note. Pentagonal inequalities and inherited cuts are standard. New here is the sharp S4 mixed-tuple separation. Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
